caption: A magnet is touched to a steel food can and holds; touched to an aluminium drink can beside it, it falls off.

sa.check: A steel food can and an aluminium drink can side by side.
A magnet is touched to the steel can and holds there.
The magnet is touched to the aluminium can.
The magnet falls off the aluminium can.
The steel can comes first and the drink can second.
The same magnet is used on both cans.

pc.expect: On the steel can the magnet stays where it is placed after the hand withdraws; on the drink can it leaves the surface as the hand lets go.
pc.fail: The magnet drops or slides down the steel can after release; or stays on the drink can with nothing holding it; or hangs a gap away from either can; or the drink can lifts away with the magnet.

pc.expect: The magnet touches the outside of each can and stays outside; the cans keep their shape; the hand passes through nothing.
pc.fail: The magnet sinks into a can; or passes through a can's wall; or a can dents deeply at the touch and stays dented; or the hand passes through a can.

pc.expect: Leaving the drink can, the magnet falls straight down and lands on the surface below.
pc.fail: The magnet drifts upward or sideways after release; or halts in mid-air; or lands and rises back to the can.

pc.expect: The cans stay where they stand; neither slides, tips or rolls on its own as the magnet is placed or falls.
pc.fail: A can slides toward the magnet; or tips over with nothing touching it; or the drink can rolls away as the magnet falls; or the magnet creeps across the steel can.

pc.expect: One magnet and two cans throughout; nothing appears, vanishes or passes through the table.
pc.fail: A second magnet appears so that one is on each can; or a can vanishes; or the magnet vanishes in mid-fall; or the magnet passes through the table.

pc.expect: The cans' labels and colours, the magnet and the surface stay the same.
pc.fail: A can's label changes; or the magnet changes colour or shape; or the surface changes.

note: P1 assumes the cans are as the caption says; a drink can that plainly reads as steel fails S1, and the magnet holding on it is then not a P1 failure.
